Class ModelLessonEditor

java.lang.Object
guiLessonEditor.ModelLessonEditor
public class ModelLessonEditor extends Object

Title: ModelLessonEditor Class.

Description: The lesson editor Model. It turns what the contributor typed into a stored lesson, either a new one (CS-1) or a change to an existing one (CS-7), and decides whether the contributor is allowed to make that change (CS-9).

As with ModelLessonsList, the decisions are kept in the Model, with no JavaFX, so the testing automation can check exactly what the editor will do with a given set of inputs. The Controller only reads the fields, calls one of the two save methods, and reports the result.

    • saveNewLesson

      public static validation.LessonInputPolicy.Problem saveNewLesson(database.LessonsLearnedDatabase db, entityClasses.LessonsLearnedList all, String userName, String title, String category, String keywords, String description, String resolution)

      Method: Problem saveNewLesson(LessonsLearnedDatabase db, LessonsLearnedList all, String userName, String title, String category, String keywords, String description, String resolution)

      Description: Creates and stores a new lesson (CS-1). The contributor is the logged in user, passed in by the Controller, never a value the user typed; in HW2 the contributor was a text field, which let anyone record a lesson in someone else's name and defeated the ownership rule before it started. Every field is trimmed, and the keywords are tidied into one standard form, before validation, so what is checked is exactly what is stored.

      Parameters:
      db - the open lessons database
      all - the shared list of every lesson, which gains the new lesson on success
      userName - the logged in username, recorded as the contributor
      title - the title typed
      category - the category typed
      keywords - the keywords typed, which may be empty
      description - the description typed
      resolution - the resolution typed, which may be empty
      Returns:
      null when the lesson was stored, otherwise the problem that stopped it

    • saveChanges

      public static validation.LessonInputPolicy.Problem saveChanges(database.LessonsLearnedDatabase db, entityClasses.LessonsLearnedList all, entityClasses.LessonsLearned original, String userName, String title, String category, String keywords, String description, String resolution)

      Method: Problem saveChanges(LessonsLearnedDatabase db, LessonsLearnedList all, LessonsLearned original, String userName, String title, String category, String keywords, String description, String resolution)

      Description: Stores a contributor's changes to an existing lesson (CS-7).

      Three things are checked before anything is written. The user must be the lesson's contributor (CS-9); the editor only offers Edit to the contributor, but the check is repeated here so that no other route can bypass it. Something must actually have changed, so pressing Save on an untouched form does not move the "last updated" date. And the new values must pass the same validation as a new lesson.

      The changes are applied to a copy, not to the original object. The original is the object in the shared list; if it were changed first and the save were then refused, the list would show values the database does not hold.

      Parameters:
      db - the open lessons database
      all - the shared list of every lesson, whose entry is replaced on success
      original - the lesson as it was read
      userName - the logged in username
      title - the title in the form
      category - the category in the form
      keywords - the keywords in the form
      description - the description in the form
      resolution - the resolution in the form
      Returns:
      null when the changes were stored, otherwise the problem that stopped them

    • tidyKeywords

      public static String tidyKeywords(String keywords)

      Method: String tidyKeywords(String keywords)

      Description: Puts the keywords into one standard form, "first, second, third", by trimming each one and joining them with a comma and a space. Duplicates, ignoring case, are dropped, so "javafx, JavaFX" is stored once. An empty entry, from two commas in a row, is left in place on purpose, so that validation can tell the user about it rather than the editor quietly changing what they typed.

      Parameters:
      keywords - the keywords as typed
      Returns:
      the keywords in standard form, or an empty string when there are none
